thread:
evan_sec: Seeing an unexpected spike (~1.6k) of TLS handshake rejects from eu-west to svc-search starting 2026-08-15T10:00Z. Logs indicate client cert CN mismatch to svc-search.

pat_sre: Paste a log sample and check KMS audit for keystore-search-euw during the nightly rotation window.

evan_sec: ingress sample:
```
2026-08-15T10:02:11Z ingress-euw-01 svc-search=\"svc-search-01\" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-search-dup, expected svc-search)
2026-08-15T10:02:12Z ingress-euw-02 svc-search=\"svc-search-02\" tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (client CN=svc-search-dup, expected svc-search)
```

mira_infra: We completed RBAC consolidation two days ago: moved explicit SA grants into group keystore-admins. There was a manual project-level grant back in 2025 that might still exist.

devex_kai: rotator runs at 03:45 UTC. The rotator should be the only principal calling KMS Decrypt during rotation. If another principal still has decrypt rights it could generate certs with the old CN.

kv-rotator-bot: rotator: rotation job keystore-search-euw-20260815-01 completed at 2026-08-15T03:45:00Z using rotator-sa@infra.redwood (job id: r-9a7d).

pat_sre: KMS audit excerpt (03:44:50-03:45:10Z):
{"timestamp":"2026-08-15T03:44:58Z","principal":"svc-search-dup@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":"projects/.../cryptoKeys/keystore-search-euw"}
{"timestamp":"2026-08-15T03:45:01Z","principal":"rotator-sa@infra.redwood","action":"Decrypt","resource":"projects/.../cryptoKeys/keystore-search-euw"}

mira_infra: That shows svc-search-dup still had decrypt permissions. Looks like an orphan project IAM binding `project.iam_member.keystore_legacy` exists in terraform state. It wasn't removed during the consolidation.

evan_sec: So the rotator and the orphan SA both decrypted; some nodes got new certs while a subset still used certs issued by the orphan SA, causing CN drift and handshakes to fail. Root cause = shadowed keystore principal.

devex_kai: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Mira remove the orphan IAM member from the KMS key policy, 2) run a canary rotation using rotator-sa, 3) run quick TLS smoke from eu-west probe to assert CN=svc-search everywhere, 4) add a monitoring alert for any KMS Decrypt by principals not in allowed_principals.

mira_infra: Removing binding now, will also queue a terraform state prune and open PR to delete the orphan entry.

kv-rotator-bot: rotator: canary rotation keystore-search-euw-20260815-canary started at 2026-08-15T03:51:00Z using rotator-sa@infra.redwood

mira_infra: Orphan binding removed @2026-08-15T10:20:41Z. Verified IAM policy no longer lists svc-search-dup.

kv-rotator-bot: rotator: canary rotation completed at 2026-08-15T03:52:30Z. New certs issued with CN=svc-search.

pat_sre: TLS probe from eu-west shows server accepts client cert with CN=svc-search and handshake succeeded. Reject rate back to baseline after 10:22Z.

evan_sec: Post-incident follow-ups: - Mira to submit PR to purge orphan terraform state entry and add a guard in CI that prevents project-level IAM overrides for keystore keys. - Security to add KMS decrypt alert rule and a weekly decrypt principals summary. - Devex to draft rotator enhancement: pre-rotation IAM sanity check that optionally aborts rotation if unexpected principals can decrypt.

mira_infra: Opening PR now. Adding a short terraform test to assert key IAM equals expected list post-apply.

devex_kai: I'll draft a tiny RFC for rotator pre-checks and make it optional for emergency overrides.

evan_sec: Filing P2 incident with root cause = keystore shadowing (orphan project-level IAM entry) after RBAC consolidation. Contributing factor = no alerting on unexpected KMS decrypt principals. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
